lessons.correction: Strengthen your ground army, increase economy and expansion, and continue technology development.
lessons.mistake: Committing to a head-on fight against Siege Tanks without proper tech or positioning, or over-expanding without sufficient army to defend.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you have more information about the opponent's army composition or expansion.
lessons.title: Avoid head-on engagement with Siege Tanks
lessons.when: Early-midgame, opponent shows heavy ground production (e.g., Marines) and you have moderate ground forces.
lessons.why: The opponent is investing heavily in ground forces, so matching their strength while growing your economy is prudent.

lessons.correction: Strengthen your ground army, increase economy and expansion, and continue technology development.
lessons.mistake: Neglecting army production while teching, or over-expanding if an attack is imminent.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when you have more information about the opponent's army composition or expansion.
lessons.title: Balance tech and army production
lessons.when: Midgame, opponent has heavy ground production (e.g., Marines) and you have a strong economy but moderate production.
lessons.why: The opponent is investing heavily in ground forces, so you need a strong army to defend while maintaining your economy.

lessons.correction: Maintain current development path with safety checks. Focus on economy and expansion while keeping options open.
lessons.mistake: Overcommitting to army before your economy is stable.
lessons.recheck: Re-evaluate when more information becomes available, such as scouting units or opponent expansion.
lessons.title: Develop economy before committing
lessons.when: Early game, opponent's posture is unknown and your own economy is still developing.
lessons.why: With limited information, it is efficient to build a solid economic foundation before committing to a specific strategy.
